DELIVERY DATE: JUNE 2002

The First Lift

The day the world opened up.

Delivery Bay 1

There was no red ribbon. There was no press. Just the humming of the factory lights and the smell of ozone and welding flux.

The "Iron Horse" (a custom Sainte-Claire 45H3) stood in the center of the bay—a massive forty-five-foot monolith finished in deep Obsidian Midnight lacquer and wrapped in sweeping Cosmic Nebula violet, cyan, and amber stardust graphics. The twenty welders and coachbuilders who had built it stood in a semi-circle, arms crossed, waiting.

Ryan O'Connell rolled onto the platform. The custom hydraulic system—over-engineered at Holly's insistence—hissed softly. He rose 60 inches into the air, the motion smooth and silent, and rolled into the main cabin.

He rolled back out onto the lift and lowered himself down. He looked at the foreman, a man named Jean-Paul.

"C'est parfait," Ryan said. "Merci, mes amis."

The applause from the crew was deafening. They weren't clapping for a client; they were clapping for one of their own.

Competitor Intelligence Report CONFIDENTIAL

SUBJECT: The "Pop Star" Order (Ref: 2002-CANCELLED)

STATUS: Total Loss.

INCIDENT TIMELINE (Aug 2002):

  • >> Subject purchased a "Luxury Coach" from a competitor in Indiana ($1.2M).
  • >> Aug 14: Driver attempted to navigate a fast-food drive-thru in Albuquerque.
  • >> Physics Failure: The uneven grade of the drive-thru lane caused "Frame Torque." Because the roof was compromised by the Jacuzzi installation, the chassis twisted.
  • >> The Leak: The fiberglass shell cracked. 200 gallons of hot water flooded the avionics bay and the master stateroom.
  • >> Warranty Claim: DENIED. Manufacturer produced a waiver signed by the artist acknowledging "Hydrodynamic Instability Risk."
  • >> RESULT: Bus scrapped. Tour cancelled.

The Stardust Engine (ERR-001)

Named after the very first song Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler wrote together at CPI in 1986—celebrating their shared love of the cosmos (“Stardust”) and the rockets to get you there (“Engine”).
